events.title: BATEYD Demo Out Now
events.summary: The BATEYD demo is live on the store page. What's in it: the opening session with your psychiatrist — the tutorial lives inside that conversation — and the first two of the game's five nightmares.A few things worth knowing before you go in. This is a game about planning, not reflexes. Everything follows rules — the Beast, its Sentinels, the fireworks, the hunger. Nothing is random, and nothing cheats. events.title: BATEYD on Steam Deck: what to expect
events.summary: BATEYD plays very well on Steam Deck, with full controller support and no on-screen keyboard ever needed. Before you start, a couple of notes on graphics settings will make it play even better. First launch on Steam DeckThe first time you launch the game on Steam Deck, it automatically sets Graphics Quality to Low. That is what guarantees a steady frame rate across the whole game. events.title: The Beast is nearly done. New screenshots, and what happens next.
events.summary: BATEYD — The Beast Awoke to Eat Your Darlings — is nearly finished.If you’re just arriving: it’s a horror game you outsmart, not survive. Everything in its nightmares runs on rules you can learn. Sentinels fire a flare when they see you. A flare always brings the Beast. A hungry Beast eats a steak before it hunts a cat. events.title: Early Build Playtest
events.summary: Today I'm going through a full playthrough! events.title: Early Build Playtest
events.summary: When you get catnip, cats follow you -- which is paramount as you need to save them! However, "cats following you" is fun only as long as you can see them. I made some changes that make this possible, from a camera that automatically gets farther away the more cats are following you, and with a cat following behavior that's more likely to get the cats on screen rather than just behind you.

events.title: Early Build Playtest
events.summary: As the game gets closer to its release date (should definitely be by the end of this year!), I'm streaming my playtests, so you can get a better idea of what it is about. Feel free to chime in, comments and suggestions are welcome!
